newsitem.title: UK: IPE oil futures edge up in directionless market.
newsitem.headline: IPE oil futures edge up in directionless market.

text.p: IPE Brent and gas oil futures edged up slightly in Wednesday afternoon trading as the market remained nervous and directionless after Tuesday's mixed U.S. stocks data, brokers said.
March Brent was trading seven cents higher at $22.50 a barrel at 1600 GMT, while February gas oil was $2.75 off at $200.25 a tonne, having slipped through $200 earlier in the day.

Dealers said the market became even more nervous after gas oil breached key resistance at $200, a psychological level which had held as resistance for five months until it briefly slipped below it on January 24.

"People are unsure after last night's API (U.S stocks data) figures - the question on these figures is does the market move lower still or were the figures priced into last night's figures and therefore the market holds and maybe bounces back," one broker said.
Dealers said heating oil was still very much driving the market and this was where the lead needed to come from if prices were to move again.
"You have to look at the products in the States to get a lead from them for the moment because volume is incredibly thin here (London), it's one of the worst afternoons for ages," another said.
American Petroleum Institute (API) data released on Tuesday was seen as having little real impact on the market as news was mixed.
The data showed a larger-than-expected draw of 4.1 million barrels on U.S. distillate stocks, but compared to year-ago levels they moved into surplus for the first time since June 1995.
There was a build of 6.06 million barrels in crude stocks.
